request.spec:
A steward can merge a grade into another (two selects and a button; GRADE_MERGED from=<grade>
into=<grade>; the same grade twice, or anyone else, is refused): every person whose grade in force
today is the merged grade is given the other from the sheet's today, each exactly as the person
form would (PERSON_EDITED and the rollup lines, in list order).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can merge a grade into another (two selects and a button; GRADE_MERGED from=<grade>
into=<grade>; the same grade twice, or anyone else, is refused): every person whose grade in force
today is the merged grade is given the other from the sheet's today, each exactly as the person
form would (PERSON_EDITED and the rollup lines, in list order).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now merge one grade into another, and the main "grade merge" test passes. Two of the other three tests in the spec still fail, but they failed the same way before my change and never use the merge.

**Results of `bin/e2e`:**
- **Passing:** "grade merge" (the test for this change) and "grade merge scenario 3".
- **Failing:** "scenario 1" stops when the restricted user `wes` quick-adds "Dot": neither a new row nor an error appears. "Scenario 2" times out waiting for `dash-pending-count` to show "0". To check these, I took the new endpoint out, rebuilt and ran the tests again: both failed at the same steps. Neither one calls the merge, so I left them alone rather than change unrelated features.

**How it works:**
- **Backend:** a new `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/grades/merge` endpoint (`grades/merge.POST.yml`) with its classes in the `grade` package. It refuses no signed-in user, the same grade twice, or anyone who isn't a steward. A refused merge writes nothing.
- **What a merge does:** it writes `GRADE_MERGED sheet=… by=… from=… into=…`. Then, in list order, everyone whose grade in force today is the merged grade gets the other one from the sheet's today. Each gets their own `PERSON_EDITED` line and rollup lines, in the same way the bulk grade action does it.
- **Extra audit lines:** the test expects one more ROLLUP/TOTALS block after all the people have been changed, covering the whole merge. I added it. Like the other rollup lines, it is only written when the figures actually moved, so the C→B merge in the test writes no rollup lines.
- **Screen:** the grades panel now has two selects (`grade-merge-from`, `grade-merge-into`), a `grade-merge` button and a `grade-merged` result ("A into B: 1"). Refusals show in the existing `grade-error`, which is now shared with the retire form and cleared when either form changes or is sent. After a merge the sheet's data is reloaded.

**Decisions you may want to check:**
- **Retired grades:** I also refuse a merge into a retired grade, because the person form wouldn't let you choose one. The request didn't say either way.
- **Same merge twice:** the result text doesn't change if you merge the same pair twice in a row. The test helper waits for that text to change, so it would report a timeout even though the merge went through. The test never does this.
- **Port:** I ran the tests with `PORT=3017`. With the default port 3000 the app failed to start, probably because another sandbox on this machine was using the port at the time.
